reason: §751 says the first Christians, by calling themselves 'Church', recognized themselves as 'heir to' Israel's assembly at Sinai, where Israel 'was established by God as his holy people'. Heirship is a stated correspondence, so preparatory is the right ceiling; the precise figure is the Sinai assembly, which the broadened 'Israel, the Chosen People' covers.

§753 says the OT images of the Church are 'variations on a profound theme: the People of God', recentred on Christ as head of this people. It teaches about Israel as People of God without naming a specific figure, so teaches-only is right.

§755 teaches the ancient olive tree 'in which the reconciliation of Jews and Gentiles has been brought about' (cf. Rom 11:17-24). No OT figure is said to prefigure the grafting, so teaches-only is the right level.

'The Lord compared himself to the stone' is a comparison, not prefigure/figure wording, so explicit is too strong. Note the stone is a psalm word (Ps 118:22) that Jesus cites as Scripture fulfilled (Matt 21:42), so the reviewer should check it is not prophecy rather than type.
'This Church was prepared in marvellous fashion in the history of the people of Israel' is exactly the preparatory wording, and Israel as a people is the figure named.

'Already present in figure at the beginning of the world' says when the Church was figured, not by what; that creation itself is the figure comes from §760 ('the world was created for the sake of the Church') and §778 ('prefigured in creation'). Keep §778 as the explicit basis and mark §759 synthesized.
'Prepared ... in the history of the people of Israel and the old Alliance' names the Old Covenant as a stage of the Church's preparation; preparatory and the td-004 Type fit.
'Its immediate preparation begins with Israel's election as the People of God ... Israel is to be the sign of the future gathering of all nations' is preparatory wording naming Israel as a people.

'The remote preparation ... begins when he calls Abraham and promises that he will become the father of a great people' is preparatory. Strictly the text names an event (the call and promise), but td-010's description is built on that call, so the person-level Type is acceptable.

'Representing the twelve tribes of Israel, they are the foundation stones of the new Jerusalem' is a stated correspondence without figure vocabulary, so preparatory is the right ceiling. The text names the tribes, which the td-002 broadening now covers.

'As Eve was formed from the sleeping Adam's side, so the Church was born from the pierced heart of Christ' is an as/so parallel with no prefigure/figure wording, so preparatory at most. The parallel pairs the sleeping Adam with 'Christ hanging dead on the cross', so christs-passion is more precise than Christ in general.

Right figure at the right precision (the event of Gen 2:21-22, not Eve the person), but the as/so parallel carries no prefigure/figure wording; the nearby 'symbolized' refers to the blood and water, not to Eve. Preparatory.
'Prefigured in creation' is explicit wording naming creation as the figure of the Church.
'Prepared for in the Old Covenant' is preparatory wording, and the td-004 Type fits.

'A preparation for and figure of' governs 'that new and perfect covenant', not the Church; the Church comes in only through the next clause ('he called together a race made up of Jews and Gentiles'). The Israel → Church link is real but synthesized; the explicit figure here is carried by the Old Covenant → New Covenant claim.

'Established a covenant with it ... All these things ... happened as a preparation for and figure of that new and perfect covenant which was to be ratified in Christ' is explicit, with covenant as type and New Covenant as antitype; Covenantal is right.

The quoted St. Augustine applies Gen 2:24 to Christ and the Church through Eph 5:31-32 ('I am applying it to Christ and the Church'): an application, not prefigure/figure wording. The 'image of bridegroom and bride' in §796 describes the Christ-Church relation, not Adam and Eve, so preparatory.

'The theme of Christ as Bridegroom of the Church was prepared for by the prophets' is preparatory; the figure is the covenant the prophets portrayed as marriage (td-021), not a prediction, so it is not prophecy. §1612 ('the nuptial covenant between God and his people Israel had prepared the way') is the stronger base.
'She is prefigured by Noah's ark' is explicit, with the ark as type and the Church as antitype.
pastoral_flag: 'Which alone saves from the flood' is a collective claim; §846 gives the Church's own reading ('all salvation comes from Christ the Head through the Church which is his Body'), cf. 1 Pet 3:20-21.

reason: 'The new Eve' is a typological title with no prefigure/figure wording in §975, so preparatory at most. Type, antitype and Marian category are right.

§994 calls the Resurrection 'the sign of Jonah', which is a real Jonah → Resurrection correspondence, but 'sign' is not prefigure/figure wording, so preparatory at most. Type, antitype and category are right.

In 'the sign of the temple' the temple stands for Christ himself, the one who 'will be put to death but rise'; the rising on the third day is Jesus' own announcement (prophecy), not something the temple figures. The temple's link here is to Christ (his body, John 2:19-21), and 'sign' supports preparatory at most.
Passover is listed among 'saving events and significant realities which have found their fulfillment in the mystery of Christ', the preparatory 'fulfilled in' wording, with Christ as antitype.

'Exile and return' are listed among the realities fulfilled in the mystery of Christ; preparatory. The text pairs exile and return as one movement, and the return Type is the right node for it (not the-babylonian-exile, whose description is polemical).
'Exodus and Passover' are listed among the realities that 'have found their fulfillment in the mystery of Christ'; preparatory, with the right Type and antitype.
'Kingdom and temple' are listed among the realities fulfilled in the mystery of Christ; preparatory, with the right Type and antitype.

'The flood and Noah's ark prefigured salvation by Baptism, as did the cloud and the crossing of the Red Sea' is explicit for the cloud. The cloud here is the Exodus cloud of 1 Cor 10:1-2, which the broadened Type covers.
'Manna in the desert prefigured the Eucharist' is explicit, with exact Type and antitype.
'The flood and Noah's ark prefigured salvation by Baptism' is explicit and names the ark.
'The flood and Noah's ark prefigured salvation by Baptism' is explicit and names the flood as a figure in its own right.
'As did the cloud and the crossing of the Red Sea' carries 'prefigured salvation by Baptism' over to the crossing; explicit.
'Water from the rock was the figure of the spiritual gifts of Christ' is explicit, with exact Type and antitype.

'The Passover fulfilled in the death and Resurrection of Christ' is the preparatory 'fulfilled in' wording. The text names the whole Paschal mystery (death and Resurrection); christs-passion is the closest existing node but covers only the death.

'The Church sees in these signs a prefiguring of the sacraments of the New Covenant' is explicit, and the antitype is rightly the sacraments in general since no specific sacrament is named. The text says 'anointing and consecration of kings and priests' (no prophets), which the existing Type covers.

§765 names the tribes, and Scripture treats the twelve sons and the twelve tribes as one twelvefold figure (Gen 49:28). The existing link → the-twelve-apostles still reads true under the broader name (Matt 19:28; Rev 21:12-14), and §765 now supports it directly.

§§759, 778, 781 name the Old Covenant, and the Sinai covenant is the covenant of the Law (Exod 24:7-8; Gal 4:24); all four existing links still read true (Matt 5:17; Heb 8:5, 10:1; Law → Gospel mirrors; Ishmael fits Gal 4:24 better). Keep the description pinned to Sinai so Noahic, Abrahamic and Davidic covenant claims (e.g. §1093 'promise and covenant') are not forced into this node.

Sound new person-level Type: the catalog lacks Abraham, and binding-of-isaac is a distinct event. §762 names God's call and promise, which the description carries; keep the 'Promise to Abraham' prophecy rows separate, as the rationale says.

One Type for the covenant the prophets portrayed as marriage is sound and distinct from Hosea (a person) and the Canticle's spouse. §796 only says the theme 'was prepared for by the prophets', so §1612's 'nuptial covenant between God and his people Israel had prepared the way' should carry the main link.

Event-level Type at the right precision, distinct from `eve` (person → Mary) and `adam-and-eve` (marriage → Christ-Church). §766's 'As Eve was formed from the sleeping Adam's side' names exactly this event.
The Kingdom 'promised over the ages in the scriptures' is promise and fulfilment (prophecy), with no OT figure named.
About the Spirit's gifts and the Church as 'seed and beginning' of the Kingdom; no OT figure.
'St. Paul calls the nuptial union of Christ and the Church a great mystery' alludes to Eph 5:32 but names no OT figure here; the Gen 2:24 link is already claimed at §796.
'The image of her poor and suffering founder' is the poor imaging Christ, a NT likeness, not an OT type; the Leo quote on Christians made kings and priests names no OT figure.

'He made human nature one in the beginning and has decreed that all his children ... should be finally gathered together as one' states God's plan from creation to gathering, without figure wording or a named OT figure.
On religious error disfiguring the image of God in man; no typology.
